pass_a_gloss: Concerning the dried fig-tree. Mark adds that from afar seeing a fig-tree having leaves he-came if perhaps he-will-find something in it; and nothing finding except leaves only (for it-was not season of figs) he-said: «No-longer into the age from you nobody fruit may-eat.» The of-the-Spirit fruits — love, joy, peace… — sometimes in own seasons are-given; but better if even of the circumstances toward the opposite to the fruit-bearing calling, someone through the much to-be-helped from the Word no-less even then may-bear the fruits. And Jesus said to the disciples: «Ask the great things, and the small will-be-added to-you; and ask the heavenly, and the earthly will-be-added to-you.»
pass_b_english: On the withered fig tree. Mark adds that seeing leaves from afar he came seeking fruit — it was not fig season — and said [[may no one ever eat fruit from you again >> Bible:Mark 11:14]]. The [[fruit of the Spirit >> Bible:Galatians 5:22-23]] is sometimes given in its own season; better still if, when circumstances push the other way, one still bears fruit because the Word has so helped. Jesus told the disciples: ask for the great things and the small will be added; ask for the heavenly and the earthly will be added.
notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
